sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill in Toms River?
sections.html:
The Township of Toms River Tax Collector bills and collects the tax, and the Tax Assessor sets the value the bill is built on. Both offices work from 33 Washington Street in Toms River, and both keep weekday hours from 8:30 to 4:30. Ocean County's Board of Taxation sits above the assessor and hears disputes over value.

Toms River has run as a calendar year town since January 2010, so the tax year follows the calendar and the bills reach mailboxes in July. If you are selling, keep that rhythm in mind: the bill you will be asked about at closing is the one for the current calendar year, split into quarters.

sections.h2: What makes Toms River a different kind of property tax town?
sections.html:
Size and shoreline. Toms River is a township on the Jersey Shore that doubles as the seat of Ocean County. It was chartered in 1768 as Dover Township and kept that name until a 2006 referendum switched it to the name of its largest community. Wikipedia lists a total area of 52.89 square miles, of which 12.34 is water, and part of the township sits on the Barnegat Peninsula, the barrier strip between Barnegat Bay and the Atlantic.

The township was the eighth most populous municipality in New Jersey in the 2020 census, at 95,438 people, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 100,899. Growth took off after the Garden State Parkway opened up the area to commuters. Students attend Toms River Regional Schools, which Wikipedia describes as the largest suburban school district in the state and which also serves Beachwood, Pine Beach and South Toms River.

For a seller, one assessor covers a wide spread of housing, from mainland neighborhoods to the Dover Beaches communities on the Barnegat Peninsula. Homes in different parts of the township can carry very different assessments, so compare your value with recent sales of similar houses nearby.

sections.h2: When are Toms River property taxes due?
sections.html:
Taxes are due on February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, with a ten day grace period after each date. The township explains that if the tenth day lands on a weekend or legal holiday you have until the next business day.

  • First quarter, due February 1, covers January through March.
  • Second quarter, due May 1, covers April through June.
  • Third quarter, due August 1, covers July through September.
  • Fourth quarter, due November 1, covers October through December.

Checks for current quarters go to a lockbox in Boston with the stub from your bill, and the township asks that you write your block and lot number on the check and send no letters with it. Payments made through a bank bill-pay service go to P.O. Box 607 in Toms River instead, and the township warns they need extra days to arrive within the grace period. An after-hours drop box at Town Hall takes tax payments only, and those post the next business day.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Toms River assessment?
sections.html:
You file an appeal with the Ocean County Board of Taxation by April 1. After a township-wide revaluation or reassessment the deadline moves to May 1. The township assessor's office directs callers to the board at 732-929-2008 for filing questions.

The assessor's FAQ is blunt about two points. An appeal challenges your assessed value and has no bearing on the tax bill, because neither the assessor nor the county board controls the budgets set by the township, school district, county or fire districts. The FAQ also says comparable assessments do not count as evidence of market value, and only comparable sales do. Gather recent sales of similar Toms River homes before you file.

If you built or added something and received an Added Assessment bill, the appeal deadline is December 1 of the year the added assessment was placed. The assessor adds that the date of the Certificate of Occupancy does not set the assessment date, because the home is valued when it is substantially ready for its intended use.

sections.h2: What deductions and relief programs does Toms River list?
sections.html:
The township tax collector's FAQ says qualified recipients receive a $250 deduction from the annual tax bill. Eligible groups are disabled persons, senior citizens, surviving spouses, veterans and widows of veterans, and applications go through the Tax Assessor at 732-341-1000, extension 8300.

The same page points homeowners to two state programs, the Property Tax Reimbursement Program and the Homestead Rebate Program. Both are state programs, so ask the state Division of Taxation about eligibility and payment status.

That mix helps explain why the senior and veteran deductions draw attention in town. The monthly cost for owners without a mortgage, $917, shows how much of a carrying cost comes from taxes and insurance alone.

sections.h2: What happens when taxes on a Toms River house go unpaid?
sections.html:
The township can sell a tax lien, and the owner or a mortgage holder can later redeem it. The Tax Collector's FAQ says only a party with legal interest, meaning the owner, the owner's attorney or the mortgage holder, may redeem, and the request must be in writing. Verbal requests are refused.

  • Include the block and lot number and the lien certificate number.
  • State the date the payment will reach the Tax Collector, no more than 30 days after the request.
  • Add a daytime phone number, then fax the request to 732-505-1886 or mail it to P.O. Box 607. Email requests are not accepted.

The redemption statement takes time to prepare, so ask well before the closing date. If a lien shows as paid but still appears in the county records, the township says you need a certificate of redemption from the county clerk, requested in writing with a $25 check for each certificate. For a sale, the title company handles the payoff, but a clean lien search starts with your own account lookup on the township's tax inquiry page.

sections.h2: How should a seller handle the tax bill at closing in Toms River?
sections.html:
Hand over the bill. The township states that no new bill is issued when ownership changes, and the bill should go to the new owner at closing. A buyer who does not receive it can request a copy from the Tax Collector or print one from the online tax inquiry.

If your mortgage company pays the taxes and the loan is paid off at closing, the township asks for written notice so it can remove the bank from its records. The notice needs the block and lot number, your mailing address, the bank's name and address, and the owner's signature. A seller who skips this step can leave a buyer with a duplicate bill and confusion over who paid the next quarter.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Toms River tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Tax Collector at 732-341-1000, extension 8342. The office is open Monday to Friday, 8:30 to 4:30, and the township warns that call volume rises around due dates. Assessment questions go to extension 8300.

faqs.q: Is there a grace period on Toms River property taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, ten days after each due date. If the tenth day is a weekend or legal holiday, you have until the next business day. Bank bill-pay payments can take several days to arrive, so send them early.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Toms River assessment?
faqs.a: April 1 of the tax year, or May 1 if the township has done a revaluation or reassessment. File with the Ocean County Board of Taxation. Added Assessment appeals are due December 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Toms River house that has a tax lien on it?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien is paid at closing from proceeds, and the owner, owner's attorney or mortgage holder must request a written redemption statement from the Tax Collector, which takes time to prepare. Ask early so the payoff figure is ready.

faqs.q: Does the new owner get a new tax bill after the sale?
faqs.a: No. Toms River does not issue a new bill when ownership changes, so the seller passes the existing bill to the buyer at closing. The buyer can print a duplicate through the township's online tax account inquiry.
